Security Equipment Sectional Committee, ME 24 


FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Security Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Divisional 
Council. 


This standard for fire resisting computer media protection cabinet covers the requirements for proper protection 
of popularly used computer media from effects of fire. Protecting computer media is of vital importance as 
retention of records through computer media has largely replaced other traditional methods like recording on 
paper, magnetic tapes, etc. The preferences for using the type of computer media have also undergone considerable 
change during the past decade. Floppy discs and compact discs are being increasingly replaced by USB drives, 
SD cards etc. It was therefore necessary to update this standard accordingly. 


This standard specifies the requirements to assess the performance of the cabinets to the limitations of 52 °C 
temperature and 85 percent relative humidity. 


This standard was first published in 1998. The major changes in this revision are: 


a) Inclusion of newer and more popular computer media for testing. 
b) Inclusion of a preliminary test to determine the ability of the media to withstand the test conditions. 


c) Restrictions of materials of construction have been removed. This has been replaced by introduction of 
strength test of shelves and assessment of fire impact test. 


d) Declaration and tolerance on weight of the cabinet have been introduced. 
e) Conditions of provisions of accessories for tests have been clarified to ensure uniformity of testing. 
f) Provisions for reporting media used in testing. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex A. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 
‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)’. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 14562 : 2014 


Indian Standard 


FIRE RESISTING COMPUTER MEDIA PROTECTION 
CABINETS — SPECIFICATION 


( First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard lays down the requirements regarding 
materials, sizes, details of construction, testing 
procedure and performance criteria of fire resisting 
computer media protection cabinets which afford 
security to computer media such as floppy disks, 
compact disks, USB drives, SD cards, portable hard 
disc, etc, against fire. 


2 NOMINAL SIZES 


Nominal sizes of the cabinet shall be denoted by its 
internal height as specified in Table 1. 


3 TYPES 


The fire resisting computer media protection cabinets 
shall be of two types as follows: 


Type FR 60 — Cabinets having a fire resisting 
capacity of 60 min. 

Type FR 120 — Cabinets having a fire resisting 
capacity of 120 min. 


4 MATERIAL 


The material for manufacturing of the product shall be 
declared at the time of type approval and records of 
the details of material which are critical to performance 
shall be maintained for conforming during routine 
production. 


5 DIMENSIONS AND TOLERANCES 


The dimensions and the tolerances of the fire resisting 
computer media protection cabinets shall be as given 
in Table 1. 


6 DESIGNATIONS 


6.1 The cabinet shall be designated by type, 
construction, nominal size and number of this standard. 
The nominal size shall be the nominal inside height of 
the cabinet. 


Example: 


A fire resisting computer media protection cabinet of 
Type FR 60, double cabinet construction and nominal 
size 400 shall be designated as: 


Fire Resisting Computer Media Protection 
Cabinet FR 60 DC x 400 


A similar cabinet of single cabinet construction shall 
be designated as: 


Fire Resisting Computer Media Protection 
Cabinet FR 60 SC x 400 


Table 1 Dimensions of Fire Resisting Computer 
Media Protection Cabinets 


(Clauses 2 and 5) 
All dimensions in millimetres. 


Nominal Size

Nominal Size 


Height of pedestal, Min 


ii) Nominal inside 
dimensions 


6.2 Cabinet of any other size can be offered by the 
manufacturer provided it complies with the design 
parameters of the sample that was tested and had passed 
the relevant tests. 


6.3 Manufacturing tolerance of 10 mm shall be 
applicable on each of the declared nominal inside 
dimensions. 


7 CONSTRUCTION 


7.1 The construction of the cabinet shall be either 
double cabinet type, that is, cabinet inside cabinet type, 
comprising of an external cabinet and an internal 
cabinet for body as well as door or a single cabinet 
type construction that is with single body and door. 


7.2 The fitment of body with the door shall be tongue 
and groove/multi-step construction type to prevent 
direct passage of flame. 


8 ASSEMBLY 


8.1 The components shall be assembled by bolting, 
welding, riveting or screwing or any combination of 
these processes. 


IS 14562 : 2014 


9 FABRICATION 


9.1 The internal cabinet shall be manufactured from 
steel or plastic or fibre-glass or wood and shall be of 
single or double wall construction. In case of steel the 
sheet thickness used for internal cabinet shall not be 
less than 0.8 mm. In case of other material, suitable 
thicknesses shall be used. 


9.2 Shelf 


Shelves shall be of adjustable type. When subjected to 
a uniformly distributed load of 2.5 kg for 30 min, no 
shelf shall show any signs of distortion or damage. 


9.3 Door 


The door shall be fabricated from steel sheet of not 
less than 1.0 mm thickness without any burrs and dents. 
For double cabinet type construction, the door of the 
internal cabinet may be made from steel sheet of not 
less than 0.5 mm thickness. 


9.4 Handle 


Handles shall be made from any material suitable for 
the purpose. 


9.5 Compression Mechanism 


A continuous resilient packing shall be incorporated 
either in door or body and a compression mechanism 
shall be provided for clenching the door tight against 
the packing, thus providing protection against 
admission of moisture inside the cabinet. 


9.6 Weight 


9.6.1 The weight of each designation of cabinet, 
without shelves and accessories if any, shall be declared 
by the manufacturer at the time of type approval. The 
weight of the sample tested for (type) approval shall 
not vary by more than + 5 percent of the declared value. 


10 SAMPLING 


Two samples known to be fully representative of a lot 
of cabinets of similar design and construction shall be 
selected on the basis of random sampling along with 
relevant design detail of the sample. 


11 TESTS 


11.1 Test for verifying fire resistant property of 
cabinets consists of fire endurance test and fire and 
impact test. For this purpose, one sample each, selected 
in accordance with 10, shall be subjected to fire 
endurance test (see 11.4) and fire and impact test 
(see 11.5) respectively. 


11.2 Test Equipment 
11.2.1 Contents 


11.2.1.1 The results of the fire resistance tests may be 
influenced by the quality and material of the computer 
media that are used as contents placed inside the 
cabinets. It is therefore essential that the resistance of 
the media to the test parameters of heat and humidity 
is ascertained before subjecting them to the actual tests. 


11.2.1.2 Contents of the fire resisting computer media 
protection cabinets subjected to these tests shall include 
three identical sets of 2 flexible diskettes, 12 compact 
discs, 4 USB drives and 4 SD cards . All the media 
shall be procured and fully recorded by the test agency. 
One set each shall be used for the preliminary test, fire 
endurance test and fire impact tests. 


11.2.1.3 One set of the media shall be placed within a 
small cabinet with provisions for maintaining an 
internal temperature of 52 + | °C and relative humidity 
of 85 + 2 percent. The arrangement shall be such that 
the temperature and humidity readings can be taken 
without opening the cabinet. The contents inside the 
cabinet shall then be subjected to the specified 
temperature and humidity for the time period for which 
the actual test specimen is to be tested (60 or 120 min, 
as applicable). On completion of this test the media 
shall be verified for their usability. Only those media 
(from the untested set ) which have been verified to be 
able to withstand the specified test parameters shall be 
used for the test of the actual cabinet sample .The 
selected media from the untested set shall be placed 
on the centre of the upper shelf and about 25 mm away 
from the lateral walls. 


11.2.2 Thermocouple 


11.2.2.1 Thermocouple enclosed in protection tubes 
of suitable material and dimensions shall have time 
constant of the protected thermocouple assembly 
within the range from 5 min to 7.2 min. A typical 
thermocouple assembly may be fabricated by fusion 
welding and twisted ends of chrome alumel wire not 
smaller than 0.52 mm square in cross section and 
mounting the leads in porcelain insulators so that the 
thermocouple head is 12 mm from the sealed end of 
the standard weight normal 12 mm diameter iron steel 
or inconel pipe. 


11.2.2.2 The provisions for installing the 
thermocouple in the cabinet may be made by the 
manufacturer, if required by the testing agency. 
However, the thermocouple assembly shall be made 
in accordance to 12.2.2.1 and installed by the testing 
agency. 


11.2.3 Humidity Measuring Equipment 


The relative humidity in the interior of the cabinet shall 
be recorded by means of electronic sensing elements 
that are accurate to within + 1.5 percent and are to 
consist of transducers having resistance that varies with 
humidity. 


11.2.4 Furnace 


11.2.4.1 The furnace fuel and air supply shall be 
adjusted such that the heat is uniformly distributed over 
the exposed faces of the cabinet and regulated to 
temperatures in accordance with the Standard Time 
Temperature Curve. 


11.2.4.2 The furnace temperature, corresponding to 
time elapsed as given in Table 2 shall follow the 
equation: 


T —T,= 345 log 10 (8 t+ 1) 


where 
T = furnace temperature, in °C at any time, 
t = time in minutes; and 
T, = ambient temperature, in °C. 


11.2.4.3 The accuracy of the furnace control shall be 
such that the area under the time temperature curve, 
obtained by averaging all the furnace thermocouple 
readings, shall be within +10 percent of the 
corresponding area under the standard time 
temperature curve, for entire test duration. 


Table 2 Relationships Between Times Elapsed and 
Furnace Temperature 


(Clause 11.2.4.2) 


SINo. Time Hapsed, min Furnace Temperature °C

ii) 10 678 
iii) 15 739

11.3 Preparations for Tests 


11.3.1 The cabinet to be subjected to fire endurance 
test shall have a 20 to 25 mm diameter through hole at 
the bottom. A pipe of the same external diameter shall 
be welded to outer and inner body sheets of the cabinet. 
This hole shall be used for insertion of thermocouple 
wires inside the cabinet. After insertion of the 
thermocouple wires through the hole it shall be sealed 
by proper insulating compound (which does not 
generate moisture on heating) from both ends of the 
hole. 


11.3.2 All thermocouples shall be located 25 mm from 
the top of the cabinet interior. Four thermocouples shall 
be located 25 mm from the side walls, two of these 
being 25 mm from back and other two 25 mm from 
the inner face of the doors. 


11.3.3 The furnace temperature shall be recorded by 
thermocouples symmetrically distributed. At least four 
thermocouples shall be used, placed 50 mm from the 
exposed faces of the test sample including the door 
face. 


11.3.4 The cabinet, to be subjected to fire endurance 
test, shall have humidity measuring sensor located 
midway from all inside surfaces. 


11.3.5 The inside temperature and relative humidity 
of the cabinet at the start of the fire test shall be 27 + 
2 °C and 85 + 5 percent, respectively. If the conditions 
in the cabinet are not within the range then it shall be 
conditioned to attain them for at least 2 h prior to the 
fire test. 


11.4 Fire Endurance Test 


11.4.1 The sample of cabinet prepared in manner 
specified in 11.3 and filled with contents as specified 
in 11.2.1 is to be locked and then placed in the furnace. 


11.4.2 The thermocouples to be placed inside the 
cabinet shall be mounted in porcelain insulators so that 
the thermocouple head is 12 mm from the sealed end 
of standard weight, nominal 12 mm diameter iron, steel 
or in-conel pipe. 


11.4.3 The furnace shall then be put on and the 
temperatures shall be read at intervals not exceeding 
5 min during the test. Average of all the thermocouples 
inside and outside the cabinet shall be recorded. 


11.4.4 The pressure in the furnace chamber during the 
test shall be maintained as close as possible to 
atmospheric pressure. 


11.4.5 The furnace fire shall be continued for 60 
minutes for FR 60 rating and 120 min for FR 120 rating. 
During the fire endurance test, it is essential that at no 
time the internal temperature of the cabinet as shown 


IS 14562 : 2014 


by the thermocouples placed inside the cabinet shall 
exceed 52 °C, irrespective of ambient temperature. Also 
at no time the interior relative humidity of the cabinet 
shall exceed 85 percent. 


11.4.6 After the specified period, the furnace is 
switched off. The cabinet is continued to be kept in 
the furnace for cooling without opening the furnace 
and temperature and relative humidity of the interior 
of the sample cabinet is to be continuously recorded 
until the temperature inside the cabinet shows a definite 
drop of atleast 3 °C by all internal thermocouples. 


11.4.7 After the cabinet, inside the furnace, has cooled 
to about 47 °C temperature, it shall be taken out from 
the furnace and its door shall be opened. The contents 
shall be examined to determine their usability in 
accordance with 11.6. 


11.5 Fire and Impact Test 


11.5.1 The cabinet to be subjected to this test shall 
have contents as specified in 11.2.1 and shall be 
subjected to test without any thermocouple and 
humidity sensors inside the cabinet. 


11.5.2 The cabinet shall be subjected to a standard 
fire exposure in a manner similar to the fire endurance 
test for the period as shown below: 


Rating of Exposure Time Reheat Time 
Cabinet in min in min 
FR 60 30 30 
FR 120 45 45 


11.5.3 After the fire exposure time, the furnace shall 
be switched off and the test sample shall be withdrawn. 
The cabinet shall then be hoisted so that its bottom is 
4 m above a layer of brick rubble (30 cm depth) on a 
heavy concrete base and then dropped. Not more than 
20 min shall be elapsed from the time the furnace fire 
is extinguished until the cabinet is dropped. 


11.5.4 After the impact, the cabinet shall be examined 
for damage. The cabinet shall not get so damaged that 
it exposes the inner contents to the outside atmosphere, 
in which case it shall be considered to have failed and 
further tests shall be discontinued. 


11.5.5 Immediately after the impact, the cabinet shall 
be inverted, put back in the test furnace and again 
subjected to a standard fire exposure for the period of 
reheat time indicated in 11.5.2. Then the cabinet shall 
be allowed to cool to less than 47 °C without opening 
the furnace. After the cabinet has cooled to less than 
47 °C, the door shall be opened to examine its heat 
insulating properties, as evident by the usability of the 
contents in accordance with 11.6. 


11.6 Criteria for Conformity 


11.6.1 The fire resisting computer media protection 
cabinets shall be considered to have successfully passed 
the fire endurance test (see 11.4) and Fire and Impact 
Test (see 11.5) if the contents (see 11.2.1, 11.4.1 
and 11.5.1) kept in the cabinet during the test are 
usable. The contents are considered to be usable after 
test if they are able to withstand ordinary handling 
without crumbling or falling apart and able to 
reproduce the data stored in them without the use of 
supplemented devices or aids of any kind. 


11.7 Test Report 


The test report issued by the agency shall invariably 
mention the make, model and other relevant technical 
details of the media which were used as contents for 
the fire endurance and fire impact tests. 


12 SURFACE FINISHING 


12.1 The inside and outside surfaces of the fire 
resisting computer media protection cabinets shall be 
painted or powder coated. In case of paint, an 
appropriate primer and undercoating shall be used in 
accordance to industry practices. The minimum overall 
thickness of the coatings shall be 50 u for powder 
coating and 70 u for liquid paint. Cross hatch test shall 
be conducted to confirm the adhesion of coating in 
accordance with 12.2. 


12.2 Cross Hatch Test 


a) Make 6 parallel cut marks using sharp metal 
pointer and straight edge, through the painted/ 
coated surface, so as to make the base surface 
visible through cut marks. 

b) Cut marks shall be minimum 20 mm long and 
at 2 mm distance from each other. 

c) Make 6 similar cut marks in the direction 
perpendicular to first set of cut marks, with 
same length and spacing. 

d) These 12 cut marks together shall make a 
pattern of 25 squares of 2 mm x 2 mm size, 
totally separated from each other. 

e) A good quality transparent adhesive tape not 
less than 20 mm width shall be stuck on the 
pattern, parallel to any one set of cut marks. 

f) To ensure continuous contact with paint/coat 
film, rub the tape firmly and remove air 
bubbles under the tape, if any. 

g) Within 60 to 120 s after sticking the tape, 
remove it by seizing free end of the tape and 
rapidly pulling it off at an angle close to 180°. 

h) Painting/Coating quality is considered as 
acceptable if no part of any 2 mm x 2 mm 
square of paint/coat comes off the surface due 
to pulling the tape. 


12.3 The finish shall be smooth and free from visible 
defects. It shall not readily chip or flake. 


13 MARKING 


13.1 A metal plate showing classification of cabinet 
together with the manufacturer’s name and the year of 
manufacture shall be fixed on the inner face of the door. 


13.2 Marking on Keys 


The key shall be marked with an identification number 
which shall not be the same as the serial number of the 
cabinet. 


13.3 BIS Certification Marking 


13.3.1 The fire resisting computer media protection 
cabinets may also be marked with the Standard Mark. 


IS 14562 : 2014 


13.3.2 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by 
the provisions of Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 
and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The 
details of conditions under which the license for the 
use of the Standard Mark may be granted to 
manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the 
Bureau of Indian Standards. 


14 PACKING 


Each cabinet shall be packed in accordance with the 
best trade practice with its door closed but not locked. 
The keys shall be separately sealed in a box or pouch 
and placed inside the cabinet. The keys may also be 
packed and dispatched separately or delivered in some 
other manner if the purchaser so requires. 


IS 14562 : 2014

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 


‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards : Monthly Additions’.
